blocks.text: Self-critique prompting has a model review its own already generated response against explicit quality criteria, accuracy, completeness, tone, and then produce a revised version, all within a single interaction, without needing the external feedback or multiple task attempts that reflection prompting, covered in the previous topic, relies on.

This topic covers how to structure a critique-then-revise sequence, why naming explicit criteria matters, the real limits of a model critiquing its own work, and when this extra step is worth the added cost.
1. What Self-Critique Prompting Means
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473225144-696298738.png

Self-critique prompting asks a model to generate a draft response, then examine that same draft critically against stated criteria, and produce an improved final version, all in one continuous interaction.
2. Self-Critique Needs No External Feedback
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473225145-477700649.png

Unlike reflection prompting, which depends on a genuine external result, a test failure, an execution error, self-critique works entirely within the model own generated text, examining a draft directly rather than needing a real world outcome to react to, this makes it applicable to a much broader range of tasks, including ones without any clear verifiable outcome.
3. Providing Explicit Criteria to Critique Against

blocks.alt: Providing Explicit Criteria to Critique Against
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473225145-552332076.png

A critique request works best when it names specific, concrete criteria, is this factually accurate, does it address every part of the original question, is the tone appropriate, a vague request to just double check your answer gives the model far less to actually evaluate against.

code.content:
prompt = (
    "First, write an answer to the question. Then, critique your own answer "
    "for factual accuracy, completeness, and clarity. Finally, provide a "
    "revised answer that addresses any issues you found."
)

blocks.text: 4. The Critique-Then-Revise Sequence
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473225767-488620346.png

The full sequence has three parts, generating an initial draft, critiquing that draft against explicit criteria, and producing a final revised version informed by the critique, each part can be requested within a single prompt or split across separate calls.

blocks.text: 5. Why Naming Specific Criteria Matters
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473225768-794522194.png

This connects directly to the specificity principle from the earlier Instruction topic, "check your work" leaves the model to decide what checking even means, "check for factual errors, missing information, and inappropriate tone" gives it concrete dimensions to actually evaluate against.
6. The Real Limits of Self-Critique
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473225769-755666073.png

A model critiquing its own output shares the exact same underlying knowledge and blind spots as the model that generated the original draft, if the model genuinely does not know a fact is wrong, its self-critique is unlikely to catch that specific error, self-critique catches inconsistencies and gaps the model can recognize, not errors entirely outside its knowledge.

blocks.title: This limitation mirrors a point made in the earlier Constitutional AI topic
blocks.content: The Fine-Tuning course Constitutional AI topic makes a closely related point, a model judging its own output inherits the same blind spots as the model generating it, self-critique in a general prompting context faces this identical limitation.

blocks.text: 7. Self-Critique Prompting vs Reflection Prompting

Self-critique and reflection, covered in the previous topic, both involve a model examining and improving its own work, the key difference is what grounds the examination, reflection uses genuine external feedback across multiple task attempts, self-critique reasons about a single draft directly, without needing an external result to react to.
8. Combining Self-Critique With Output Format and Constraints

Self-critique combines naturally with output format and constraints, both covered in earlier topics, explicitly asking the critique step to check whether the draft actually satisfies the stated length constraint or output format specification gives the technique concrete, checkable criteria beyond just general quality.
9. When Self-Critique Is Worth the Extra Step

blocks.alt: When Self-Critique Is Worth the Extra Step
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473225769-336159272.png

Self-critique adds a genuine extra generation step, worth the added cost specifically for complex or high stakes outputs where catching an inconsistency or gap before it reaches a user actually matters, for simple, low stakes responses, the added step provides little benefit relative to its cost.
Worked Example
A developer generates a draft explanation of a technical concept directly, without any critique step, and later notices it fails to address one part of the original multi part question.

Adding a critique step, explicitly asking the model to check whether its draft addresses every part of the original question, catches this exact gap, and the revised version produced afterward correctly addresses the previously missed part, all within the same interaction and without needing any external feedback signal.
Common Mistakes

items: Asking for a vague, unspecific critique instead of naming concrete criteria like accuracy, completeness, or tone
Assuming a self-critique will catch a factual error the model did not actually know was wrong in the first place
Applying self-critique to every simple, low stakes response regardless of whether the extra step is actually needed
Confusing self-critique, which reviews a single draft directly, with reflection, which depends on genuine external feedback

blocks.text: Practice

Take a response you have generated before without a critique step, add an explicit critique request naming specific criteria relevant to that task, and compare whether the resulting revised version genuinely improves on the original draft.
Key Takeaway

Self-critique prompting has a model review its own draft against explicit, named criteria and produce a revised version, all within a single interaction, catching inconsistencies and gaps the model can recognize, though it shares the same underlying blind spots as the model that produced the original draft, making it a useful but imperfect quality check.
